disclaimer: Paper trades only: research/lottery/NFA. No real execution, no wallet keys, no real sizing. Nothing here is a profit claim.

paper_ticket_conversion.note: Re-convert at each new ticket; existing tickets keep their entry conversion.

levels.3: Watch: lots of holders early that stick through first dip
levels.4: High-conviction lottery: L3 + cross-platform/bigger accounts, improving SOL-side pool, holder growth through first dip, prior similar shapes worked in paper book

thresholds.status: initial guesses, to be learned from the paper book; revise only with a dated rule entry
thresholds.scale_note: Pump.fun runs ~5-15x Solada's holder counts and ~4-8x its pool depth in USD terms; thresholds scaled accordingly.

L3.flow: h6 buys > sells AND h1 buys >= sells
L3.first_fade: has had a >=30% pullback from post-graduation high, price still >=40% of that high, holders not bleeding (>=-3% vs prior snapshot)

thresholds.farm_filter_L1: Any of: >=10 identical balances among pump.fun top-50; GeckoTerminal holder count <10% of pump.fun count (or vice versa); liq/mcap <2%; h6 buy:sell count >5:1 with sub-$1 fills; clone txn counts across tickers => Pass (sybil/wash).
thresholds.kill_line_default: mcap -30% from entry OR holders -10% from entry OR pool quote side -30% from entry OR full exit by any identified first-block sniper/bundler wallet
thresholds.selection: 5-10 names per run (recent graduates/near-graduates + GeckoTerminal/pump.fun trending); paper-trade L3+ plus the run's strongest L2; max 2 new tickets per run; no duplicates (one open ticket per mint).

rules.rule: Watch (L3) needs early holder density that holds through the first fade (>=1,500 holders after a >=30% pullback, no holder bleed); an mcap spike alone isn't enough.
rules.title: Watch needs 1,500+ holders after a 30% pullback

rules.rule: Graduation alone isn't a signal; on Pump.fun most graduates bleed or are farmed. Score the post-migration PumpSwap pool, not the graduation event.
rules.title: Score the PumpSwap pool, not the graduation

rules.rule: Price rising with flat holders = Tiny lottery (L2) at best.
rules.title: Rising price on flat holders caps at Tiny lottery

rules.rule: First-block snipers/bundles (same-slot-as-create buyers, or pump.fun isSniper/isBundler flags) = rotation risk; >20% of supply bought in the create slot caps the name at L2.
rules.title: Create-slot snipers and bundles cap a name at L2

rules.rule: First-block sniper/bundle full exit = kill trigger; if already hit before entry, no ticket (a paper entry shouldn't open below its own kill line).
rules.title: Exit when first-block snipers or bundles sell out

rules.rule: Paper tickets need a meaningful holder base (>=500 L2 / >=1,500 L3), pool depth (>=85 / >=200 SOL quote side) and buys > sells over h6 (and h1 for L3). Names with h6 price down >40% are Pass regardless of 24h headline gains.
rules.source: mirrored from solada-paper.json, scaled to Pump.fun
rules.title: Tickets need holder base, pool depth and h6 flow

rules.rule: Sybil/wash farm filter: identical balances across many top holders, holder-count mismatch between sources, liq/mcap <2% or lopsided tiny-fill buy counts = Pass. RST, TRUTH, SARP (and GDF/XBC/GOIF/DNA/UDTF/FTR-fire clones) showed this on Oct 17.
rules.title: Identical balances or source mismatches mean sybil farm

rules.rule: Copycat tickers (several FTR mints live) mark peak attention for the original; don't ticket a copy because the original ran.
rules.title: Copycat tickers mark peak attention for the original

rules.rule: Reactivation spikes don't qualify even as the strongest L2: CyberAxe (+1,271% h1 on a 66h coin) hit its kill within ~2h (-31.7%) even though holders rose 1,512 -> 1,710. Require one full hourly candle holding above the spike's midpoint before ticketing.
rules.title: Reactivation spikes need a held hourly candle first

rules.rule: Counts aren't flow: 'h6 buys > sells' only counts if h6 price change is >= -10%. FTR kept a buy-count majority (4,645/3,353, then 2,665/1,584) while falling 34% h6 into its kill. Close a ticket early when holders fall at two marks in a row and price is below entry (FTR 18,434 -> 18,111 -> 17,599) instead of waiting for the -30% line.
rules.title: Exit after two holder drops below entry

rules.rule: Sybil holder band: on a coin under 24h old, 10+ of the top-12 non-pool holders sitting within about +/-10% of each other is a sybil/bundled distribution even when balances aren't exactly identical. MINTER (4h old, 7,512 holders, $3.8M) had all top-12 at 0.24-0.27% (Helius). Treat it as L1, whatever the holder count.
rules.title: Tight top-holder balance band means sybil distribution

rules.rule: Old coins need fresh holders: on coins older than 7 days, the strongest-L2 ticket also needs holder growth of 2%+ between two snapshots. swordcat (19 days old) went 9,939 -> 9,932 -> 9,930 holders and closed -11.6% under pf-m.
rules.title: Coins older than 7 days need fresh holder growth

rules.rule: Farm filter refinement: on coins under 2 hours old, an average fill under ~$5 is a wash/bot farm even when buy and sell counts are balanced (the >5:1 test misses these). Tonight Claude AI (22,994/17,095 txns on $58k = ~$1.4 fills), FOMO (~$1.3), Mr Beast (~$1.7, 45 identical top balances) and LEGO (~$3.9) all showed it. rules.title: After a pf-m exit, re-check before calling it right
rules.rule: pf-m early exits so far: CATE closed at -0.3% (11:12 PM Oct 18) and kept sliding (~$69.0M -> $66.95M by 7:50 AM), so that exit was right. Dacity closed at -16.8% (5:15 AM, $3.95M, holders 5,650 -> 5,640 -> 5,617) and by 7:50 AM was back to $4.43M (-6.7% vs entry) with holders 5,656, above the pre-drop count. A two-mark dip of under ~1% of holders on a 5k+ holder coin can be noise. Keep pf-m, but log every pf-m exit's price and holders at the next run; if two more exits recover like Dacity, raise pf-m's trigger to a 1% cumulative holder drop on coins with 5,000+ holders.

rules.title: Only count a holder mismatch when both counts are fresh
